rationale: C01 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. It uses nearly the same distinctive enumeration of tax-return types and the same operative machinery: the returns “shall be open to inspection,” followed by conditions stated in a related Treasury decision approved by the President on the same date. The child adapts that established sentence structure from congressional inspection to inspection of accepted compromise offers and related papers. C09 and C12 share essentially the same machinery and tax enumeration, but C01 is the strongest displayed antecedent because it is closer in time and its wording aligns especially closely with the child's full list.

shared_material.child_excerpt: income, excess profits, declared value excess profits, capital stock, estate or gift tax returns for any taxable year shall be open to inspection
shared_material.parent_excerpt: any income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, capital stock, estate or gift tax return for any period to and including 1951, shall ... be open to inspection
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive, nearly complete tax-category enumeration combined with the same operative command opening returns to inspection.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Such inspection shall be subject to the conditions stated in the related Treasury decision approved by me this date.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: subject to the conditions stated in the Treasury decision relating to the inspection of such returns by that Committee, approved by me this date.
shared_material.explanation: The child reuses the same administrative mechanism tying inspection authority to conditions in a contemporaneously approved Treasury decision.
